<thought>Using the ESI mass spectrum, the base peak at m/z 235.139 likely corresponds to the [M+H]⁺ ion. Subtracting the proton mass gives a neutral monoisotopic mass of ≈ 234.13 Da. The isotopic pattern (≈ 16 % M+1 and ≈ 4–5 % M+2) points to a molecule containing about 13–15 carbons and a single sulfur atom (S gives a characteristic ~4 % M+2). A formula that matches the mass and isotopic pattern is C₁₃H₁₄O₂S (monoisotopic mass ≈ 234.07 Da, [M+H]⁺ ≈ 235.08 Da, close to the observed m/z). Therefore the molecular formula is C13H14O2S.</thought>
<final_answer>C13H14O2S</final_answer>
